note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 33-year-old female returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago presenting with 7 days of fever, night sweats, chills, systemic myalgia, nausea, poor oral intake and fatigue.
- Plan made for face-to-face clinic examination and blood tests including thick and thin films for malaria; advised not to work until investigation completed.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute febrile illness for 7 days: intermittent high temperature, hot sweats, night sweats, alternating hot and cold periods, generalized muscle aches, nausea with reduced appetite and reduced oral intake, pronounced fatigue.
- Systems review: denies cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, new or severe headache, rash, joint swelling, or urinary symptoms.
- Relevant history: returned from travel to Vietnam 4 weeks ago with rural exposure (trekking, cycling, farmland); patient reports taking malaria prophylaxis but cannot recall drug name; believes it was a daily regimen and that she took an additional tablet on top of the first (patient uncertain about exact regimen).
- Examination findings: none documented in this consult (face-to-face exam planned).
- Specialist/allied review and differential: clinician concerned about malaria and other travel-related or usual infections; plan for in-person review to guide urgency of investigations.
- Investigations recommended: thick and thin blood films for malaria, inflammatory markers and other blood tests as directed by examining clinician.
- Work advice: advised not to attend work until cause is clarified.

Issue 2:
- Chronic low back pain: long-standing, related to prolonged sitting and poor posture.
- Treatment: currently under physiotherapy with posture and strengthening exercises.
- No acute joint swelling or new focal musculoskeletal findings reported in this consult.

Issue 3:
- Ongoing mental health treatment / headaches and allergies:
  - On Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Chronic headaches related to screen use and weather; no acute severe headache or migraine reported today.
  - Allergy: pollen (hay fever).

Medications:
- Seroxat — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen — over-the-counter; dose/route/frequency not documented (patient taking recommended OTC dosing).
- Paracetamol (acetaminophen) — over-the-counter; dose/route/frequency not documented (patient taking recommended OTC dosing).
- Malaria prophylaxis — drug name not documented; patient unsure, believes it was daily and that an additional tablet was taken on top of the first.

Allergies:
- Pollen (hay fever).
- No drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic low back pain.
- No other major illnesses volunteered.

Social History:
- Occupation: nurse; currently finding work difficult due to fatigue/illness.
- Smoking: non-smoker.
- Alcohol: moderate intake.
- Exercise: moderate exercise a few times per week.
- Living arrangements: not discussed.

Preventative History:
- States vaccinations are up to date, including hepatitis B.
- No documentation of cervical screening, mammogram, prostate test, FOBT, bone density, or recent optometry/skin checks in this consult.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination findings documented in this consult; face-to-face exam arranged.

Plan:
- Immediate: arrange face-to-face clinic appointment for clinical examination.
- Investigations: request thick and thin blood films for malaria and inflammatory markers; additional blood tests as indicated by examining clinician.
- Logistics: doctor to send note to admin to book patient into central London clinic today; patient may alternatively attend local A&E and present this note.
- Work: advised patient not to return to work until investigations initiated and cause clarified.
- Follow-up: clinician in clinic to determine urgency of tests and further management after examination; results/further plan to be communicated thereafter.
